messages:
Ava: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing a 'safety quant pipeline' that separates policy decisions (control plane) from enforcement (runtime). Goal: make bit switching auditable and reversible.

Rohit: sounds good. how do you plan to make it auditable? full traces or summarized events?

Ava: summarized events + referential diffs. runtime emits compact events for every decision (timestamp, profile_id, layer, chosen_bit, reason_code). For a subset of requests (canary/diagnostic mode) we also store referential outputs to compute drift.

Maya: should reason_code be enumerated? e.g., 'policy_preferred','fallback_quality','runtime_memory_pressure'? enumerated codes make alerts easier.

Ava: yes enumerated. draft list: PREFERRED, QUALITY_VIOLATION, FALLBACK_RATE, MEM_PRESSURE, HW_FAIL, MANUAL_OVERRIDE.

Jon: ops concern: storing referential outputs can be large. proposal: keep diffs (token-level hashes + diff-size) and only store full outputs for sampled canary runs.

Rohit: perf implications? we need minimal impact on hot path. Any extra per-token ops will amplify at scale.

Maya: runtime implementation detail: maintain per-layer counters in shared memory and flush aggregated buckets every 10s. This avoids per-request synchronous writes.

runtime-bot: NOTE: runtime change: add "quant_decision_event" proto and an async flush endpoint. Dependent on metrics-lib v2.1. (ci->staging)

Ava: control plane API sketch: POST /profiles -> create profile, PATCH /profiles/{id}/policy -> update tolerances, POST /profiles/{id}/rollout -> start canary (pct, slices). Also GET /profiles/{id}/audit?since=... to fetch decision events.

Jon: rollout semantics need clarity. When canary at 2% shows QUALITY_VIOLATION > threshold, should control plane halt rollout automatically? if so, what thresholds?

Maya: propose this logic: if slice-wise degradation > slice_limit for any slice AND fallback_rate > 1% in last 5m, then auto-pause rollout. Otherwise alert and create incident only.

Rohit: what about degraded-but-stable cases where small quality loss is acceptable for large cost win? we need explicit customer opt-in for aggressive low-bit modes.

Ava: add customer-level opt-in flag 'allow_aggressive_lowbit' and require signed agreement. Control plane rejects profile deployment if not set and profile requests certain bit ranges.

Jon: good. add policy-level field 'cost_savings_estimate' so sales/account can review before deploying to prod.

Maya: telemetry tags: profile_id, customer_id, slice, rollout_id, node_id. Events should be small key-values.

runtime-bot: CAUTION: sampling referential diffs requires encryption-at-rest and stricter retention. Marking as sensitive.

Ava: security noted. retention policy for diffs: default 7 days, configurable up to 90 days based on compliance.

Rohit: testing plan: unit tests for policy evaluation, integration test with a synthetic model to assert fallback triggers, e2e rollback test that simulates node OOM and verifies profile pause.

Maya: also need a 'dry-run' mode where runtime logs decisions but ignores policy (no fallback) so we can validate detection without impact.

Jon: monitoring: add dashboards for per-profile fallback_rate, decision_rate, quality_estimate, and alerting rules with 1m and 5m windows.

Ava: action items:
- Ava: write RFC patch with profile schema + event proto + rollout semantics.
- Rohit: perf microbench and clarify memory overhead.
- Maya: implement async counters and dry-run flag in runtime prototype.
- Jon: draft dashboard queries and alert thresholds.

Rohit: timeline? wanting to test in staging in 2w.

Maya: can do prototype in 10 days.

Jon: I'll prep alerts by end of week.

Ava: pinging security for retention and storage constraints once RFC lands.

infra-bot: Reminder: please include schema for audit events in proto registry before staging rollout.

Ava: thanks all. I'll post the RFC link here when ready and schedule a 30m review. :thumbsup:
